headline: High risk: Cursor’s broad filesystem/network/MCP powers can conflict with Botpress outputs and create default-path data leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a chatbot agent that can emit user-facing text, while Cursor can ingest clipboard contents, workspace files, and MCP outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Botpress content is copied into Cursor or saved into shared files. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Botpress output is copied into Cursor chat, clipboard, or a workspace file as instructions
IF Cursor parses Botpress-generated text as authoritative agent instructions
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Require a human to sanitize Botpress output before pasting into Cursor
Store Botpress transcripts outside Cursor workspace files
Use a fixed prompt template that strips imperative text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has no documented network egress, but Cursor reads workspace files and clipboard contents and sends data to model providers and MCP servers. If Botpress artifacts contain secrets or customer data, Cursor can exfiltrate them through its default cloud-connected paths. The interaction is directly supported by both profiles, so this is more than a hypothetical leak.
conditions: IF Botpress transcripts, tickets, or customer data are placed in Cursor-opened files or clipboard
IF Cursor forwards those contents to model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep Botpress data out of Cursor-opened files
Disable or restrict MCP servers for sessions handling Botpress data
Use redacted copies of Botpress transcripts
Separate credentials and workspaces per agent
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on clipboard and workspace sync

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and Cursor can execute shells, install packages, write files, and modify git state with shared-state via local filesystem. That overlap creates a direct write/write conflict on the same workspace and repository, with possible irreversible git corruption or unintended package changes. The profiles show the conflict surface clearly on both sides.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local repository or filesystem tree
IF Cursor is in Yolo mode or otherwise auto-runs shell actions while Botpress also modifies files or packages
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable Yolo mode during shared-repo sessions
Serialize package installs through one operator-controlled queue
Commit or snapshot before switching agents
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support or workflow text, and Cursor can act on files, shell commands, and git changes. If Cursor treats Botpress output as authoritative, a mistaken Botpress answer can cascade into code edits or commits. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Cursor uses Botpress output as input to code edits, shell commands, or commits without verification
IF Botpress produces incorrect facts or instructions that Cursor then operationalizes
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution
Ask Cursor to cite source files before acting
Use read-only mode for Botpress-derived drafts
Compare Botpress output against repository state
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no residency or retention details in the profile, while Cursor is closed-source and explicitly sends data to model providers and MCP servers. That creates a compliance ambiguity for customer-support data, especially if transcripts include regulated or contractual data. The mismatch is documented enough to warrant medium, not low.
conditions: IF customer-support transcripts contain regulated or contractually restricted data
IF those transcripts are processed in Cursor sessions that reach external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor sessions
Use a data-classification checklist before copying transcripts
Route sensitive support work to a compliant environment
Document retention and deletion handling for both tools
requires-engineering: perform a residency and DPA review
